description: Integrated marketing retainer proposal for a fast-growing premium non-alcoholic beverage brand.
provenance: Modeled on annual agency-of-record proposals for consumer brands: growth diagnosis, audience strategy, channel plan, measurement, campaign calendar, team model, fees, and performance governance. Deliberately exercises a nine-slide deck with a media-mix pie chart, commercial KPI cards, and concrete FY2027 campaign economics.

document.presentationTitle: FY2027 Integrated Marketing Retainer — Ember Tonic

content.title: FY2027 Integrated Marketing Retainer
content.subtitle: Prepared for Ember Tonic | November 5, 2026 | Northline Brand Partners

content.title: Turn national availability into repeat household penetration.
content.subtitle: Growth mandate
prose: Eight metros represent 58% of authorized doors and 64% of current velocity.
National creator and retail-media layers reinforce those priority markets.
Northline unifies strategy, creative, social, shopper, analytics, and production.

content.title: What the data says
content.subtitle: FY2026 sales, shopper-panel, and brand-tracking diagnosis
bulletPoints: All-commodity volume grew 38%, but 71% of growth came from new distribution rather than same-store velocity
Unaided awareness is 6% nationally and 14% in the Pacific Northwest; the leading premium competitor is at 19%
First purchase converts strongly: 42% of trial households repeat within 90 days versus 31% for the category
Taste and low sugar drive purchase; functional-ingredient messaging is remembered but rarely changes choice
Retail search share is 4.8% despite 9.2% shelf share in authorized natural and premium grocery doors
Creative testing shows the bottle and serving ritual outperform abstract wellness imagery by 27% on purchase intent

content.title: From product proof to a repeatable brand platform
content.subtitle: Current marketing pattern versus the proposed FY2027 system

content.title: FY2027 commercial objectives
content.subtitle: Joint targets; retail outcomes measured in priority metros

content.title: Working media follows the consumer from discovery to shelf
content.subtitle: Recommended FY2027 working-media allocation of $7.8M

content.title: Campaign calendar — one platform, four commercial moments
content.subtitle: Creative system designed for reuse across brand, retail, and earned channels
bulletPoints: January-March — Dry January and awards-season hosting: establish the evening reset ritual and seed bartender credibility
April-June — Spring table campaign: retail displays, creator dinners, and national food-and-design earned media
July-September — Summer social occasions: chilled serve, outdoor sampling, and priority-metro out-of-home
October-December — Holiday trade-up: gifting, hosting bundles, retailer exclusives, and premium search capture
Always-on — community management, retail media, search, sampling conversion, and monthly creative optimization
Innovation support — two flavor launches receive naming, packaging hierarchy, launch assets, and retailer sell-in materials

content.title: Retainer, production, and ways of working
content.subtitle: Twelve-month agency-of-record engagement beginning January 4, 2027
bulletPoints: Integrated strategy and account retainer — $165,000 per month covering named cross-functional team capacity
Creative development and studio production fund — $1.35M annually, governed through quarterly scopes
Creator management fee — 12% of contracted creator spend; creator compensation paid at cost with audit rights
Media planning and buying fee — 7% of managed media; no undisclosed rebates or inventory ownership
Quarterly performance holdback — 8% of retainer tied equally to delivery, brand-lift, and retail-velocity milestones
Initial term of 12 months; termination for convenience after month six with 90 days' notice

content.title: Appoint Northline by November 30 for Dry January.
content.subtitle: Proposed next steps
prose: November 16: data handoff and retailer calendar workshop.
December 1: team mobilization; December 14: production begins.
